1: /**
2:  * Rules engine: modifier transparency + mechanical-effect application, no dice simulation.
3:  *
4:  * By explicit product decision (see HANDOFF.md), this app does not roll dice for the player —
5:  * it tells them what to roll (2d6 + Virtue, plus every modifier and where each one comes from)
6:  * and, once they report back which tier they hit (or a physically-rolled d6 for a formula like
7:  * "1d6 + Mettle"), applies the resulting mechanical change to the sheet. The randomness always
8:  * happens at the table, on real dice.
9:  */
10: import { newId } from './logic.js';
11: import type { Ability, AbilityEffect, CharacterSheet, CharacterStatus, Library, StatusPolarity } from './types.js';
12: 
13: // ---------- Roll modifier breakdown ----------
14: 
15: export type RollModifierKind = 'Virtue' | 'Condition' | 'Status' | 'Ability';
16: 
17: export interface RollModifierSource {
18:   Label: string;
19:   Value: number;
20:   Kind: RollModifierKind;
21: }
22: 
23: export interface RollBreakdown {
24:   VirtueId: string;
25:   VirtueName: string;
26:   Sources: RollModifierSource[];
27:   Total: number;
28: }
29: 
30: /** A RollBonus Ability effect whose Duration isn't 'Permanent' depends on a fictional trigger
31:  *  (`TriggerText`) this engine has no way to evaluate on its own — surfaced separately so the
32:  *  player can decide by hand whether it applies right now, rather than silently guessed at. */
33: export interface ConditionalRollBonus {
34:   Label: string;
35:   Value: number;
36:   TriggerText: string;
37: }
38: 
39: function applicableRollBonusEffects(abilities: Ability[], abilityIds: string[], virtueId: string, moveId?: string): AbilityEffect[] {
40:   const owned = abilities.filter((a) => abilityIds.includes(a.Id));
41:   const effects: AbilityEffect[] = [];
42:   for (const a of owned) {
43:     for (const e of a.Effects) {
44:       if (e.Kind !== 'RollBonus') continue;
45:       const targetsVirtue = !e.AppliesToVirtueId || e.AppliesToVirtueId === virtueId;
46:       const targetsMove = !e.AppliesToMoveId || e.AppliesToMoveId === moveId;
47:       if (targetsVirtue && targetsMove) effects.push(e);
48:     }
49:   }
50:   return effects;
51: }
52: 
53: /** "What to roll" for a given Virtue: base score, Condition penalty (floored, same rule as
54:  *  `effectiveVirtueScore`), the single highest helpful and highest hindering Status (only the
55:  *  highest of each counts — see the Statuses rule), and any always-on (`Permanent`) Ability
56:  *  RollBonus. Pass `moveId` to also pick up move-specific bonuses (e.g. "+2 Ongoing to Sway the
57:  *  Spirit"). */
58: export function computeRollBreakdown(sheet: CharacterSheet, virtueId: string, library: Library, moveId?: string): RollBreakdown {
59:   const vv = sheet.Virtues.find((v) => v.VirtueId === virtueId);
60:   const virtue = library.virtues.find((v) => v.Id === virtueId);
61:   const cond = library.conditions.find((c) => c.VirtueId === virtueId);
62:   const sources: RollModifierSource[] = [];
63: 
64:   const base = vv?.Score ?? 0;
65:   sources.push({ Label: virtue?.Name ?? 'Virtue', Value: base, Kind: 'Virtue' });
66: 
67:   let flooredVirtue = base;
68:   if (vv?.ConditionMarked && cond) {
69:     sources.push({ Label: `${cond.Name} (marked)`, Value: cond.RollPenalty, Kind: 'Condition' });
70:     flooredVirtue = Math.max(base + cond.RollPenalty, library.settings.ConditionFloor);
71:   }
72: 
73:   const helpful = [...sheet.Statuses].filter((s) => s.Polarity === 'Positive').sort((a, b) => b.Rank - a.Rank)[0];
74:   const hindering = [...sheet.Statuses].filter((s) => s.Polarity !== 'Positive').sort((a, b) => b.Rank - a.Rank)[0];
75:   if (helpful) sources.push({ Label: `${helpful.Name} (highest helpful Status)`, Value: helpful.Rank, Kind: 'Status' });
76:   if (hindering) sources.push({ Label: `${hindering.Name} (highest hindering Status)`, Value: -hindering.Rank, Kind: 'Status' });
77: 
78:   for (const e of applicableRollBonusEffects(library.abilities, sheet.AbilityIds, virtueId, moveId)) {
79:     if (e.Duration === 'Permanent') {
80:       sources.push({ Label: `Ability bonus${e.TriggerText ? ` (${e.TriggerText})` : ''}`, Value: e.Value ?? 0, Kind: 'Ability' });
81:     }
82:   }
83: 
84:   const extra = sources
85:     .filter((s) => s.Kind === 'Status' || s.Kind === 'Ability')
86:     .reduce((n, s) => n + s.Value, 0);
87: 
88:   return { VirtueId: virtueId, VirtueName: virtue?.Name ?? virtueId, Sources: sources, Total: flooredVirtue + extra };
89: }
90: 
91: /** Ability RollBonus effects that *might* apply but need the player's own judgment call (their
92:  *  Duration isn't 'Permanent') — shown alongside the breakdown above, not folded into its Total. */
93: export function conditionalRollBonuses(sheet: CharacterSheet, library: Library, virtueId: string, moveId?: string): ConditionalRollBonus[] {
94:   return applicableRollBonusEffects(library.abilities, sheet.AbilityIds, virtueId, moveId)
95:     .filter((e) => e.Duration !== 'Permanent')
96:     .map((e) => ({ Label: e.AppliesToMoveId ? 'This move' : `${e.Duration} bonus`, Value: e.Value ?? 0, TriggerText: e.TriggerText ?? '' }));
97: }
98: 
99: // ---------- Resist Rolls ----------
100: 
101: /** Matches `MoveResults`' own tier keys (Tier3 = 10+, Tier2 = 7-9, Tier1 = miss) so a Resist
102:  *  Roll's outcome is reported the same way a Move's is. */
103: export type RollTier = 'Tier3' | 'Tier2' | 'Tier1';
104: 
105: /** Resist Roll: roll + relevant Virtue. On a hit, the incoming Status Rank is reduced by the
106:  *  Virtue score used (10+ reduces one further); on a miss, no reduction — the incoming Rank
107:  *  lands in full. A negative Virtue score can't make a resist roll *worse* than a miss, so it's
108:  *  floored at 0 before the tier bonus is added. Some Statuses are GM-flagged non-resistable and
109:  *  simply never reach this function. */
110: export function resistRollReduction(virtueScoreUsed: number, tier: RollTier): number {
111:   if (tier === 'Tier1') return 0;
112:   const base = Math.max(0, virtueScoreUsed);
113:   return tier === 'Tier3' ? base + 1 : base;
114: }
115: 
116: // ---------- Status engine ----------
117: 
118: /** Ranks 1-5 are normal; a Negative Status that would reach this Rank is Subdued instead of
119:  *  simply sitting at "Rank 6" — the doc describes the scale as 1-6 but enforces a functional
120:  *  cap of 5, with the 6th mark meaning overflow, not a bigger version of the same thing.
121:  *  Matches `GameSettings.StatusMaxRank` (6) by default. */
122: export const DEFAULT_SUBDUED_RANK = 6;
123: 
124: export interface StatusApplyResult {
125:   Statuses: CharacterStatus[];
126:   /** True when this application pushed a Negative Status to `maxRank` — the caller should run
127:    *  the Subdued flow (see `resolveSubdued`/`resolveRiskDeath`) rather than just display Rank 6. */
128:   Subdued: boolean;
129: }
130: 
131: /** Gives (or increases) a Status by name+polarity. An existing Status with the same Name and
132:  *  Polarity has its Rank increased by the incoming amount ("mark the next empty box to the
133:  *  right"); otherwise a new Status is created. Capped at `maxRank` — see `DEFAULT_SUBDUED_RANK`. */
134: export function giveStatus(
135:   statuses: CharacterStatus[],
136:   incoming: { Name: string; Polarity: StatusPolarity; Rank: number },
137:   maxRank: number = DEFAULT_SUBDUED_RANK,
138: ): StatusApplyResult {
139:   if (incoming.Rank <= 0) return { Statuses: statuses, Subdued: false };
140:   const existing = statuses.find((s) => s.Name.toLowerCase() === incoming.Name.toLowerCase() && s.Polarity === incoming.Polarity);
141:   const rawRank = (existing?.Rank ?? 0) + incoming.Rank;
142:   const subdued = incoming.Polarity !== 'Positive' && rawRank >= maxRank;
143:   const cappedRank = Math.min(rawRank, maxRank);
144: 
145:   const next = existing
146:     ? statuses.map((s) => (s.Id === existing.Id ? { ...s, Rank: cappedRank } : s))
147:     : [...statuses, { Id: newId('st'), Name: incoming.Name, Rank: cappedRank, Polarity: incoming.Polarity, LinkedToIds: [], AffectedByIds: [] }];
148: 
149:   return { Statuses: next, Subdued: subdued };
150: }
151: 
152: /** Clears Ranks off a single existing Status (healing, a successful Resist Roll's reduction,
153:  *  etc.) — fully clearing removes the Status entry, matching the sheet's existing Pip behavior. */
154: export function healStatus(statuses: CharacterStatus[], statusId: string, amount: number): CharacterStatus[] {
155:   if (amount <= 0) return statuses;
156:   return statuses
157:     .map((s) => (s.Id === statusId ? { ...s, Rank: Math.max(0, s.Rank - amount) } : s))
158:     .filter((s) => s.Rank > 0);
159: }
160: 
161: /** Opposite Statuses can't coexist — giving one cancels Rank-for-Rank against a Status the
162:  *  player/GM identifies as its opposite (e.g. Friendly 2 into an existing Hostile 3 leaves
163:  *  Hostile 1; the reverse leaves Friendly 1; an exact match clears both). There's no authored
164:  *  "opposite pairs" registry yet (Statuses are free-text — see `StatusesPanel`), so the caller
165:  *  supplies which existing Status this one opposes rather than it being inferred from the name. */
166: export function applyOpposingStatus(
167:   statuses: CharacterStatus[],
168:   incoming: { Name: string; Polarity: StatusPolarity; Rank: number },
169:   opposingId: string,
170: ): CharacterStatus[] {
171:   const opposing = statuses.find((s) => s.Id === opposingId);
172:   if (!opposing) return giveStatus(statuses, incoming).Statuses;
173:   const net = opposing.Rank - incoming.Rank;
174:   const withoutOpposing = statuses.filter((s) => s.Id !== opposingId);
175:   if (net > 0) return [...withoutOpposing, { ...opposing, Rank: net }];
176:   if (net < 0) {
177:     return [...withoutOpposing, { Id: newId('st'), Name: incoming.Name, Rank: -net, Polarity: incoming.Polarity, LinkedToIds: [], AffectedByIds: [] }];
178:   }
179:   return withoutOpposing;
180: }
181: 
182: // ---------- Subdued / Scar / Risk Death / Blaze of Glory ----------
183: 
184: export type SubduedChoice = 'Scar' | 'RiskDeath' | 'BlazeOfGlory';
185: 
186: /** Matches RollTier's 10+/7-9/miss shape for the "roll + Nothing" Risk Death roll. */
187: export type RiskDeathOutcome = 'Tier3' | 'Tier2' | 'Tier1';
188: 
189: export interface RiskDeathResult {
190:   Outcome: RiskDeathOutcome;
191:   /** The Subduing Status's new Rank on a clean live result; null when the character is taken
192:    *  out of the scene (unconscious or dying) rather than just knocked back down. */
193:   SubduingRankAfter: number | null;
194:   RequiresScar: boolean;
195:   Narrative: string;
196: }
197: 
198: export function resolveRiskDeath(outcome: RiskDeathOutcome): RiskDeathResult {
199:   switch (outcome) {
200:     case 'Tier3':
201:       return { Outcome: outcome, SubduingRankAfter: 3, RequiresScar: false, Narrative: 'You live. The Subduing Status drops to Rank 3.' };
202:     case 'Tier2':
203:       return {
204:         Outcome: outcome,
205:         SubduingRankAfter: null,
206:         RequiresScar: true,
207:         Narrative: 'You live, but are unconscious or taken out of the scene. The GM assigns a Scar — accept it, or the character perishes.',
208:       };
209:     case 'Tier1':
210:       return { Outcome: outcome, SubduingRankAfter: null, RequiresScar: false, Narrative: 'Dying. Narrate your last words.' };
211:   }
212: }
213: 
214: export function makeScar(text: string, at: string): { Id: string; Text: string; At: string } {
215:   return { Id: newId('scar'), Text: text.trim(), At: at };
216: }
217: 
218: // ---------- Recoveries ----------
219: 
220: /** Formula given for Healing a Status: 1d6 + Mettle, spending a Recovery. Since this engine
221:  *  never rolls dice itself, `d6Rolled` is the number the player reports rolling physically. */
222: export function healingSurgeAmount(d6Rolled: number, mettleScore: number): number {
223:   return Math.max(0, d6Rolled) + mettleScore;
224: }
